title: Newsom Appoints Indian American Ajay Bhutoria to California Engineering Board
excerpt: The Fremont tech leader and former Biden AANHPI commission member will serve as a public member of the California Board for Professional Engineers, Land Surveyors and Geologists.
body:
• California Governor Gavin Newsom has appointed Indian American civic and technology leader Ajay Bhutoria to the California Board for Professional Engineers, Land Surveyors and Geologists.
  • Bhutoria, a Fremont resident, has more than two decades of experience in enterprise technology and software architecture, and has led Global Business Consulting Services since 2006.
  • He previously served on President Joe Biden's advisory commission on Asian Americans, Native Hawaiians and Pacific Islanders, and was deputy national finance chair of the Democratic National Committee from 2022 to 2024.
  • Bhutoria has been a prominent advocate for legal immigration reform, including recapturing more than 230,000 unused green cards and eliminating per-country caps.

California Governor Gavin Newsom has appointed Ajay Bhutoria, an Indian American technology executive and civic leader from Fremont, to the California Board for Professional Engineers, Land Surveyors and Geologists, according to an announcement from the Governor's office. Bhutoria will serve as a public member of the board, and the appointment does not require confirmation by the California State Senate.

A powerful licensing board

The board operates under the California Department of Consumer Affairs and regulates the practice of engineering, land surveying and geology across the state. Its responsibilities include setting licensing standards and overseeing professional practice intended to protect life, health, property and public welfare. The body licenses the professionals whose work underpins California's built environment, from bridges and buildings to land boundaries and geological assessments.

Public members play a distinct role on such boards: they are not licensed practitioners but citizens charged with representing the public interest in how professions are regulated. Bhutoria said he plans to bring his experience in artificial intelligence, emerging technologies and process improvement to the position, signaling an interest in modernizing how the board operates.

"Deeply honored to be appointed by @GavinNewsom to the California Board for Professional Engineers, Land Surveyors & Geologists! I look forward to advancing the Board's mission to protect public safety while leveraging AI to streamline processes & modernize state governance for all."

— Ajay Bhutoria, on LinkedIn

Two decades in enterprise technology

Bhutoria has spent more than 20 years in enterprise technology, software architecture and public service. Since 2006, he has served as founder and principal of Global Business Consulting Services, advising Fortune 500 companies and public-sector institutions on digital transformation, human resources technology and enterprise system administration, according to American Bazaar Online.

He earned a Bachelor of Technology degree in Chemical Engineering from the National Institute of Technology, Tiruchirappalli, before building a career in Silicon Valley as a technology leader, author and civic advocate.

From the White House to Sacramento

The Sacramento appointment extends a long record of civic engagement. Then-President Joe Biden appointed Bhutoria to the President's Advisory Commission on Asian Americans, Native Hawaiians, and Pacific Islanders, where he served during the Biden administration advising the White House on equity and opportunity for AANHPI communities.

His political leadership includes service on the Obama National Finance Committee, as co-chair of the Asian American Council Finance Committee for Hillary Clinton's 2016 presidential campaign, on the National Finance Committee for Joe Biden's 2020 campaign, and on the Harris for President National Finance Committee in 2024. From 2022 to 2024, he served as deputy national finance chair of the Democratic National Committee. According to American Bazaar, he has spearheaded national multilingual voter outreach, helped launch the White House AANHPI Economic Summit series, and worked to strengthen small-business growth and the U.S.-India relationship.

Immigration advocacy and the diaspora stake

Bhutoria has also been one of the more visible Indian American advocates for legal immigration reform. As reported by India-West, he has pushed proposals to recapture more than 230,000 unused green cards, address employment-based green card backlogs, eliminate per-country caps, and streamline H-1B visa and employment authorization processing. He has also advocated a 60-day grace period for displaced technology workers and championed domestic H-1B visa renewal reforms and immigrant civil rights.

These are kitchen-table issues for the Indian American community, which accounts for the largest share of H-1B visa holders and faces the longest employment-based green card queues under the per-country cap system. His appointment places a figure sympathetic to those concerns in a California regulatory leadership role, even though the engineering board's remit is licensing rather than immigration policy.

What to watch

The immediate question is how Bhutoria's technology agenda translates inside a licensing body: whether his push to use AI to streamline processes and modernize governance produces faster, more transparent licensing for engineers, surveyors and geologists. Board meetings are public, and his early votes and proposals will show how a public member with a Silicon Valley background approaches a traditionally practitioner-dominated regulator.
